facts.title: Bermuda Has the Northernmost Coral Reef System in the Atlantic
facts.summary: Bermuda has the northernmost coral reef system in the Atlantic Ocean, at about 32.4°N, far north of where reef-building corals usually grow.

facts.title: Bermuda Is Called the Shipwreck Capital of the Atlantic, With Over 300 Wrecks
facts.summary: Bermuda is known as the shipwreck capital of the Atlantic: more than 300 sunken ships, dating from the 1600s to 1997, lie in the waters around the island.

facts.title: The British Virgin Islands' Waters Hold Nearly 480 Recorded Marine Fish Species
facts.summary: FishBase, the global fish database, lists 477 marine fish species in 103 families for the British Virgin Islands, so the popular figure of "over 300" understates what has actually been recorded.

facts.title: Clownfish Can Change Their Sex From Male to Female
facts.summary: Clownfish are protandrous hermaphrodites: a breeding male can turn into a female, but a female never turns back into a male.

facts.title: Fiji Is Known as the Soft Coral Capital of the World
facts.summary: Fiji is widely billed as the soft coral capital of the world, a title its reefs earn with walls and pinnacles draped in brightly coloured soft corals.

facts.title: Grand Cayman Has a Rare Bioluminescent Bay Near Rum Point
facts.summary: A bay in Grand Cayman's North Side district, near Rum Point, glows at night because its water is packed with bioluminescent dinoflagellates.

facts.title: Greenland Sharks May Live for Centuries, Longer Than Any Other Known Vertebrate
facts.summary: The Greenland shark is the longest-lived vertebrate known, with a lifespan estimated at between 272 and about 510 years.

facts.title: The Remote Cocos (Keeling) Islands Have Surprisingly Rich Marine Life
facts.summary: The reefs of the Cocos (Keeling) Islands in the Indian Ocean support a surprisingly rich mix of marine life for such a small, remote place.

facts.title: The Ocean Produces About Half of Earth's Oxygen
facts.summary: Roughly half of the oxygen produced on Earth comes from the ocean, mostly from plankton: drifting plants, algae and some photosynthetic bacteria too small to see with the naked eye.

facts.title: The Remote Cocos (Keeling) Islands Hold an Estimated 414 Million Pieces of Plastic
facts.summary: The beaches of the remote Cocos (Keeling) Islands in the Indian Ocean are littered with an estimated 414 million pieces of plastic weighing about 238 tonnes.

facts.title: The Ocean Makes Up About 99% of the Living Space on Earth
facts.summary: Measured by volume, the ocean makes up about 99% of the living space on Earth, according to the United Nations.

facts.title: Stingray City Lets Visitors Stand Among Wild Southern Stingrays
facts.summary: Stingray City is a series of shallow sandbars in Grand Cayman's North Sound where visitors can stand in about 3 feet (1 metre) of water surrounded by wild southern stingrays.

facts.title: Dean's Blue Hole in the Bahamas Plunges 202 Meters Deep
facts.summary: Dean's Blue Hole, in a bay west of Clarence Town on Long Island in the Bahamas, drops to a depth of 202 meters (663 feet).

facts.title: The Cayman Islands Have Been Fighting a Lionfish Invasion Since 2008
facts.summary: The Cayman Islands have been fighting an invasion of lionfish, a venomous predator from the Indo-Pacific, since the first one turned up in local waters in 2008.

facts.title: The Cayman Islands Have About 140 Recorded Shipwreck and Maritime Sites
facts.summary: The Cayman Islands National Museum has recorded 140 maritime sites, shipwrecks among them, across Grand Cayman, Cayman Brac and Little Cayman.

facts.title: The Bottom of the Mariana Trench Is Just Above Freezing
facts.summary: At the bottom of the Mariana Trench, nearly 11 kilometers down, the water stays at about 1 to 4 °C (34 to 39 °F), just a few degrees above the freezing point of fresh water.

facts.title: The Deepest Point in the Ocean Is Deeper Than Mount Everest Is Tall
facts.summary: The Challenger Deep, at the southern end of the Mariana Trench in the western Pacific, is about 10,935 meters (35,876 feet) deep, the deepest known point in the ocean.

facts.title: The Cocos (Keeling) Islands Are Built From Coral, Not Volcanic Rock
facts.summary: The low islands of the Cocos (Keeling) Islands are made of coral material rather than volcanic rock: sandy reef islands sitting on a platform of cemented coral boulders and other skeletal debris.

facts.title: The RMS Rhone Is a Famous Wreck Dive in the British Virgin Islands
facts.summary: The RMS Rhone, a Royal Mail steamship wrecked off Salt Island in the British Virgin Islands on 29 October 1867, is one of the territory's best-known dive sites.

facts.title: The Tallest Waterfall on Earth Is Hidden Beneath the Ocean
facts.summary: The world's largest known waterfall is underwater, beneath the Denmark Strait between Greenland and Iceland.
